library: landing-page-swipe-file 2026-09-29, trimmed 2026-10-01 (8 Parker accounts, 14 pages); plus 1 Parker house build (tpj-gruns-1, 2026-10-01)

templates.name: Reasons-why listicle
templates.use_when: Many creators and angles feed one page, and the buyer needs several reasons, not one. Works for Exploration into early Evaluation.
templates.story: A numbered article that feels like content. Each reason is one benefit with one piece of proof and its own button, so a reader can leave for the product at the moment they are convinced. The Perfect Jean sends most of its traffic to a standalone 10 reasons page; Rugiet runs the same template for two products; mindbodygreen makes the last reason "results build over months" to sell the bigger plan.

refs.brand: The Perfect Jean (Parker build, Grüns style)

sections.job: State the discount and that it is already applied
Make it read like an article from a real person
sections.guide: name, title (relatable, 2-6 words), updated (month year); only a real author or the brand's own editorial name

sections.job: Headline that states the page's promise as N reasons (the named ad's promise, when there is one)
sections.guide: headline: "N reasons [who] [love/switched to] [product]" or "Why [expert type] recommend [product] for [problem]", 6-14 words, in the buyer's words (keep the ad's voice when an ad is named); subhead: one-line product truth, 10-20 words; bullets: 3 proof points of 3-8 words; cta: 2-5 words; image: product in use

sections.job: Show the win against named or typical rivals at a glance
sections.guide: columns: criterion + us + 1-2 rivals; 4-6 rows of short cells; note: one-line TL;DR, 8-20 words; only true, sourced rival facts

sections.job: One benefit, one proof, one button per reason
sections.guide: 5-10 items; title 4-10 words; body 25-60 words with one number or proof; cta 2-5 words, a different verb each time; order: core benefit or speed first, fit or range, reviews and repeat buying, guarantee, lasting results, price vs rivals, zero risk or social payoff last

sections.job: One big proof number and a short quote
Borrow authority
sections.guide: only real press or institutions on record

sections.job: Close with the offer, what's included and the risk reversal
sections.guide: product_name; options 1-3 (plan or bundle) with price and anchor from the allowlist; includes 3-6 items; gifts only if real; cta 2-5 words; guarantee 6-15 words

sections.job: Short headlined reviews
Answer the last objections
Keep the claim button in reach

templates.adaptation: No named rivals on record: compare against "typical [category]" with facts the brand can back, or drop the table. No author: drop the byline rather than invent one. A brand with one strong reason should not use this template.
templates.watch_outs: Every button goes to one link with the discount already applied. Standalone (no site menu) beat on-store at The Perfect Jean. Review counts must match across the ad and the page (TPJ showed four different counts).

templates.name: Founder-story long page
templates.use_when: Problem-aware, older buyers who have tried everything; the product has a mechanism story and the founder is the proof. Clone it per symptom or audience.
templates.story: A long sales letter that sits in the problem first. The founder lived it, tried everything the reader has tried, found the mechanism, and turned it into an easy form. Proof, a timeline, who it is not for, and a buy box that prices every freebie. Primal Queen puts over half its top spend behind one of these and clones it for each symptom.

sections.job: Name the offer (and its end, if urgency is allowed)
sections.guide: text 6-12 words; countdown only if urgency_allowed and the date is real

sections.job: Name 2-3 symptoms the reader lives with, promise the easy form
sections.guide: headline 8-16 words naming symptoms; subhead 12-25 words (old answer, new format); cta 2-5 words; trust: customer count, rating, guarantee length, shipping (allowlisted); image: product or founder with product

sections.job: Five one-line wins, each a different benefit
Who I am and what it cost me
sections.guide: heading 4-10 words; 2-4 paragraphs of 30-70 words; one specific scene

sections.job: "I tried everything": the alternatives the reader has tried
sections.guide: heading 3-8 words; list the 5-8 alternatives in one or two paragraphs

sections.job: The mechanism, and why you can't just take it raw
Proof by numbers
What to expect and when
sections.guide: 4-5 steps (1 week, 1 month, 3, 6 months); what 6-16 words each; only claims the brand may make

sections.job: Us vs the common alternative
Who it's for and who it's not for
sections.guide: for: 3-4 items; not_for: 2 items; each 4-12 words

sections.job: Subscription default, every freebie priced, guarantee
sections.guide: options 1-3; gifts with dollar values only if real; guarantee 6-15 words; cta 2-5 words

sections.job: Safety, fit with other products, sourcing, timing, guarantee
Founder sign-off: a month from now
sections.guide: heading 4-10 words; body 25-60 words; cta 2-5 words

templates.adaptation: No founder story on record: this template is the wrong pick, use lp-03 (first-person) or lp-01. No before/after rights: drop it, never simulate. Urgency banned: the offer bar states the offer without a clock.
templates.watch_outs: Long pages suit 45+ buyers who read; keep sentences plain. Health brands keep every claim inside the approved wording.

templates.name: Advertorial
templates.use_when: There is a known rival to beat, or the audience trusts editorial more than ads. Head-to-head rounds or an "I tried it" first-person story.
templates.story: It looks like an article. A byline, a disclosure, a problem the reader recognises, then either rounds against the rivals with a winner after each, or a first-person story from doubt to result. Every round or turn ends with a button carrying the code. Rugiet runs several of these on review-style sites.

sections.job: Label it honestly
sections.guide: Sponsored / advertorial line and partnership disclosure

sections.job: A real writer or reviewer
sections.guide: name, title, updated; reviewer only if a real named expert reviewed it

sections.job: Article headline in the reader's words
sections.guide: headline: "[You] vs [Rival]: which [category] actually works?" or "I tried [product] for [problem]", 8-16 words; subhead 10-25 words; image

sections.job: Top pick box up front
sections.guide: heading 2-6 words; points 2-3 of 4-10 words; cta with the code

sections.job: Intro: how common the problem is and who tested
What to look for: criteria that match the product's mechanism
Side by side, winner highlighted
Rounds (head-to-head) or story beats (first person), each ending in a button
sections.guide: 3-5 items: title 3-8 words; body 40-90 words; winner line 3-10 words (head-to-head only; concede one honest tie); cta 2-5 words

sections.job: Overall winner or result
sections.guide: heading 3-8 words; points 3 of 5-12 words; cta

sections.job: Search-style questions

templates.adaptation: First-person mode: rounds become beats (the problem, failed fixes, discovery, doubt, first use, a full-day test, result) with no winner lines. No real writer or reviewer: use the brand's own editorial name and say so in the disclosure; never invent a person.
templates.watch_outs: The article must cover the same product and angle as the ad (Honeylove's Popdust piece did not). Rival claims must be sourced and current; date the comparison.

templates.name: Product page built for ads
templates.use_when: The buyer already wants the category. The decision happens in the buy box, so put the offer and the risk reversal there, on an ad-only URL or price.
templates.story: Not the store's product page: a custom version with the buy box at the top, an ad-only price or offer, a risk reversal under the button, and proof blocks in the order a nervous first-time buyer needs them. Honeylove and Laura Geller each put their biggest page spend behind one.

sections.job: The exact offer or code (the named ad's, when there is one)
Hero buy box: name, what's inside, rating, anchor to ad price, options, risk reversal
sections.guide: heading: product name + category claim 4-10 words; rating_line allowlisted; options 1-3; includes 3-5; guarantee or try-first line 6-15 words; cta 2-4 words; image

sections.job: "Perfect for": 3-4 buyer problems in their words
Press or awards on record
Us vs an unnamed typical competitor
Clinical or testing proof
Results timeline
Why I made this / why we let you try it
Reviews, ideally tagged by time used
Choosing the variant, will it suit me, how to use, returns

templates.adaptation: No ad-only price: the offer bar carries the ad's code or offer instead. No risk reversal: use the standard guarantee; never invent a trial.
templates.watch_outs: The offer on the page must match the ad exactly (Open Farm's ad promised WELCOME20; the page never showed it).

templates.name: Offer lander
templates.use_when: The ad sells a specific trial, free gift or limited drop. The headline is the offer, word for word.
templates.story: A short, standalone page that opens on the ad's own value line and sells one offer: a $10 trial, a product plus a free gift, a limited variant. Harry's runs at least four test versions behind one URL; Laura Geller's version drops the site menu entirely.

sections.job: Review strip or offer line
The offer's value line as the headline (the ad's own line, when an ad is named), the offer as the button
sections.guide: headline 4-10 words (the offer line, or the named ad's line); subhead 8-20 words (pain relief); cta names the offer, 3-6 words; trust: shipping and money-back; image: product or kit

sections.job: Four short promises
Who it's for: three specific frustrations
sections.guide: for: 3 items of 5-12 words; not_for optional

sections.job: Offer card: price, anchor, savings, what's in the kit or the gift choice
sections.guide: options 1-3; includes 3-6; gifts with values if real; cta 3-6 words

sections.job: Headline proof stat
Price comparison vs a named rival, dated
sections.guide: 3-5 rows; note carries the source and date

sections.job: Three short reviews on the main pain
Offer terms and product questions
Final call to action with the price stack

templates.adaptation: Limited drop: add the 'almost gone' line only if stock is really limited. Free-gift offer: the buy box lists gift options with their values.
templates.watch_outs: Test the page like an ad: Harry's rotates story, engineering and value versions behind one URL.
